title: Wanderer above the Sea of Fog
theme: sublime, solitude, contemplation, human smallness before nature

interpretations.text: Caspar David Friedrich's Wanderer above the Sea of Fog shows a solitary figure standing on a rocky peak, back turned, gazing into a sea of mist and distant mountains. It is a Romantic image of the sublime: the self confronting vast nature and the limits of knowledge. The fog suggests uncertainty; the upright stance suggests resolve. Philosophically it speaks to solitude, inwardness, and the search for meaning at the edge of what can be seen or controlled.

The mood is contemplative and awe-struck rather than triumphant. The viewer shares the wanderer's vantage yet cannot see his face, which invites projection: ambition, doubt, freedom, or loneliness. It suits themes of personal journey, clarity after struggle, and standing alone with one's thoughts.
Vertical rocky foreground, soft horizontal bands of fog, cool greys and muted greens, silhouette of a man in a frock coat. Strong figure-ground contrast; atmosphere over detail.
